cs.t: ThinkPad T530 or W530 with the 1920x1080 screen upgrade. The W530 is marginally heavier but cheaper in some configurations and takes 32GB instead vs the T's 16GB. Install an aftermarket Samsung 830 (not 840) SSD if you have the money. The 840 uses cheaper flash chips than the 830, which is a top quality SSD. ThinkPad build quality is unrivaled. The keyboard is almost as nice as my HHKB. The hinges are rock solid. The keyboard has drainage ducts. Everything is designed to be serviced.
cs.th: Ask HN: Which developer laptop should I buy?

cs.t: Intel had a superior product with the Gen 1 SSDs, back when the competitors were mostly shipping with buggy controllers that would randomly brick or have hideous performance issues. Intel never followed up on their SSD controllers for the second generation though, and instead just bought the same chips everyone else did, eliminating any advantage in buying the Intel drive.  Samsung stovepipes their SSD manufacturing and have managed to put out a superior product.
cs.th: Intel discontinues Joule, Galileo, and Edison product lines

cs.t: As someone who owns a T420, I can recommend it for that price. The CPU might be a bit slower and battery life might not be as good as a modern notebook but the keyboard is extremely nice and the overall performance with an SSD is good even for modern workflows. Just be sure to not use a Samsung 840 Evo SSD, I had bad experiences with stutter during heavy I/O that didn't happen with an HDD or Samsung 950 Pro. You can also upgrade the memory by yourself, if you need to. Remember to check if the T420 has an Nvidia Quadro card inside. If it does, the Display Port is wired to the Nvidia card and works badly under Linux and sucks the battery dry quite fast.
cs.th: Ask HN: Which laptop for development?

cs.t: I used my Note 4 for three years and it's still in perfect shape, aside from the headphone jack. I've got several of their SSDs, they're all good so far. I just got a scratch and dent 2017 year entry level Samsung TV running Tizen, the UI is much faster than what I've seen on other devices. My Samsung microwave had issues within the first year, a local service depot sent a person to the house to fix it. I don't like their choices deviating away from Android to the degree I won't buy their handsets anymore, but have no complaints about them otherwise and think a lot of their hardware and design is very good.
Samsung has been my goto for SSDs but even they're swapping chips on the same SKU. At least Intel hasn't engaged in this shitfuckery. Are there any other good guys in storage these days?
